question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Sib-pair split experiment to test whether survival is heritable: Expand a clone, then split sister cells into parallel wells and treat each separately, varying the time between split and treatment from hours to weeks. If survivor frequency is correlated between sisters at short delays and decorrelates at long delays, that quantifies how long the surviving state is remembered and separates heritable priming from moment-to-moment randomness.
2. Expressed lineage barcodes plus paired profiling of untreated relatives: Transduce cells with heritable, transcribed barcodes, then sequence both a drug-treated arm and an untreated arm sampled before treatment so that the ancestors and cousins of future survivors can be identified retrospectively. Comparing the pre-treatment molecular profiles of clones that go on to survive versus those that die points directly at the primed state rather than at post-treatment adaptation.
3. Live imaging of signaling and cell-cycle reporters through drug addition: Image cells carrying kinase-activity and cell-cycle reporters (for example ERK, AKT, CDK2 sensors) continuously from before dosing until survivors are visible, then trace each survivor backwards through the movie. This reveals whether survival is predicted by baseline pathway activity, by a quiescent or slow-cycling phase at the moment of exposure, or by how fast signaling rebounds after inhibition.
4. Chromatin and transcription factor state of rare pre-primed cells, with causal follow-up: Apply single-cell ATAC-seq or joint RNA/ATAC profiling to untreated populations and to survivors, looking for a rare subpopulation whose regulatory landscape already resembles the resistant end state. Candidate transcription factors nominated this way can then be tested causally with CRISPR activation or inhibition to see whether raising or lowering their frequency shifts the fraction of cells that survive.
5. Pooled genetic screens layered onto the surviving fraction: Run CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi, or ORF overexpression screens in the presence of drug and score which perturbations change the number of survivors rather than bulk growth, including screens performed on survivors to find dependencies specific to that state. This distinguishes genes that set how often the surviving state arises from genes required to maintain it once entered, and nominates combination treatments that collapse the surviving fraction.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Single-cell drug exposure and target engagement, not just signaling state
ideas.description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates and how much target it actually engages — using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, lysosomotropic and efflux-pump reporters, cell volume/dry mass from quantitative phase imaging, and a single-cell target-engagement readout (e.g. NanoBRET or a phospho-substrate immunofluorescence dose curve) — then ask whether survivors are simply the cells that received the lowest effective dose. This tests the mundane but rarely excluded possibility that 'tolerance' is pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (sequestration, efflux, surface-to-volume, cell cycle–linked volume changes) rather than a primed regulatory state, and it sets the baseline any molecular model must beat.

ideas.title: Hidden copy-number heterogeneity from extrachromosomal DNA and mis-segregation in 'isogenic' cells
ideas.description: Perform single-cell DNA sequencing plus DNA-FISH for the target gene and known resistance loci on untreated cells, survivors, and regrown colonies, scoring extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) copies, focal amplifications, and whole-chromosome aneuploidy per cell. Because ecDNA segregates randomly at mitosis, it generates heritable, rapidly reversible dosage variation that mimics epigenetic priming — so quantifying its distribution before treatment, and whether survivors are drawn from the upper tail, decides whether the phenomenon is genomic at all before any chromatin explanation is invoked.

ideas.title: Survival as a neighborhood property: spatial statistics plus engineered context
ideas.description: Map the spatial coordinates of every survivor relative to local pre-treatment cell density, colony edge, and the positions of neighbors that died, testing for clustering beyond what clonal relatedness predicts; then control the variable directly with micropatterned islands of defined size, transwell separation, and medium conditioned by drug-killed cells. This asks whether the surviving fraction is partly set by paracrine signals released during apoptosis and by local crowding — a determinant that single-cell dissociation-based assays systematically destroy, and one that predicts survivor frequency should be tunable by plating geometry alone.

ideas.title: Apoptotic threshold and mitochondrial inheritance rather than upstream signaling
ideas.description: Profile the death machinery itself at single-cell resolution — BH3-peptide-induced cytochrome c release or MOMP timing imaged live, together with per-cell mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, and BCL-2-family protein levels — and track how unevenly mitochondria and these proteins are partitioned between daughters at each division. If survivors come disproportionately from the daughter that inherited the less-primed mitochondrial pool, survival is a downstream execution threshold with a short, division-generated memory, which predicts that lowering the threshold with a BH3 mimetic collapses the surviving fraction without touching any upstream pathway.

ideas.title: Tune expression noise while holding the mean fixed, as a causal test
ideas.description: For a candidate determinant, build isogenic lines expressing it from synthetic promoters or degron/feedback circuits that give matched mean levels but deliberately different cell-to-cell variability, and titrate global noise modifiers as an orthogonal arm; then measure survivor frequency across the panel. Most causal follow-ups shift the average level of a factor, which cannot distinguish 'more of X helps' from 'variability in X creates the rare cells that survive' — this design separates the two, and a quantitative prediction follows: survivor frequency should scale with the variance, not the mean.
